title: REVIEW: Loved revisiting this classic show in such an intimate space!...
transcript: And Ben back with another theater review. Today we are talking ragtime at the Signature Theater in Arlington, Virginia. This was my first time at the Signature Theater. I have so many friends who love this theater and swear by the work that they do. So I was really excited to check out this production. And in many ways I think this was the perfect for show to see at signature, because not only was it really great, but it was also the perfect representation of one of the things that signature does best, and that is producing traditionally large scale shows in a very intimate venue. In Ragtime's case, they had a 33 person cast and a 16 piece orchestra in a theater that seated probably no more than 300 people. And so being able to see the show at this scale in this intimate a venue was really such a treat. And I think that ragtime is one of the greatest American scores in musical theater canon. I definitely have a couple of issues with the book of the show, particularly the fact that they have crammed so much plot into the two and a half hour show that I think it does feel bloated and rushed at times. But the score, in my opinion, more than makes up for any shortcomings in the book and especially this production and this cast. I wanna give a special shout out to Teal Wicks who is mother. She also plays The character of mother in the show, I was absolutely floored by her performance. This is some of the best acting I have ever seen from her and her back to before absolutely broke my heart. I also wanted to shout out Awa Salseka who played Sarah in this production. She's a performer I was not familiar with before seeing this show, but is definitely one to keep your eye on cause she was incredible in the show. Was also super impressed with the directing work by Matthew Gardner. He had a really deceptively difficult task taking a show like Rag Time that was basically written to be on a giant stage and translating that to work in a much smaller theater. I think a smaller standing set could have felt very limiting in the hands of another director, but he really makes the most of it. And he also uses the intimacy to his advantage, allowing his performers to give more grounded and nuanced performances than they would typically be able to give in a 2,000 seat theater. The result is a rag time like I have never seen before, and it really made me see several months in the show through a completely new lens. Unfortunately, this production only runs through this weekend and is completely sold out. So if you wanna see it, you're probably out of luck. But there is good news and that is that they still have some really great shows coming up. I'm Really excited about Private Jones and Penelope. And they're also doing a revival of hair, which I think, especially in this venue, is going to be really, really cool. But as for right time, I'm gonna give it 4.5 out of 5 stars. I loved this production. I love this show, and I am so glad I got the opportunity to go down to Virginia and see it.
